archetype.name: Game Manager (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A 14-year journeyman who wins by staying on schedule: quick, short throws, few sacks, few risky balls, and an offense that has to do the heavy lifting around him.

report.headline: A competent emergency arm whose good day came with ideal conditions
report.take:
Case Keenum is the Bears' third quarterback, listed as QB3 on the depth chart and Out on the site, behind a Caleb Williams who has started every game since Week 6. His 2026 is two appearances: a full, clean start against Philadelphia in Week 3 and a relief cameo at Green Bay in Week 5 when he played a third of the snaps. That is too little to call a season. It is enough to read what he still is at 38.8.

The Philadelphia game is the version of Keenum that works. He was 24 of 34 for 247 yards and two touchdowns with no sacks and +0.189 EPA per dropback. He got the ball out in 2.41 seconds on 6.4 intended air yards, was pressured on only 8.6% of dropbacks, and Ben Johnson's structure did much of the work. Under center he was nearly perfect: 14 plays at +0.643 EPA with an 85.7% success rate. From shotgun he was at -0.301 over 41 plays. Play-action and under-center timing throws over the middle are where he lives. He was +0.34 EPA per play to the middle and -0.365 to the right, and +0.584 on 11 intermediate attempts. That Eagles defense now ranks 25th, and Chicago led most of the day.

Green Bay showed the other side. Behind on the scoreboard against a defense now ranked 9th, he held the ball 3.08 seconds, was pressured 18.2% of the time, threw 31.6% bad balls, and finished with an interception, a lost fumble, two sacks and -5.3 EPA on 19 throws. His splits say the same thing in aggregate: +0.293 EPA per play within one score, -0.463 when trailing by nine or more. The deep ball isn't there either, with one completion on four 20-plus attempts.

The career explains the split personality. 2017 in Minnesota (+0.174 EPA per play, 11th) was the outlier. Most of his seasons sit in the bottom half, and his last action before this year, 2023, was -0.265. The low sack rate, which ranks 3rd, and the tidy interception count are real and long-standing traits. They come from a quick, conservative release, not from playmaking. He keeps a scheme on schedule. He doesn't carry one.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks with quick release
strengths.body: His 3.6% sack rate ranks 3rd, and he was pressured on just 12.7% of dropbacks, 2nd-lowest. That comes from a quick, short-area style and has held across his career. It's a dependable trait in a structured offense.

strengths.title: Under-center timing and play-action
strengths.body: From under center he was 13 of 14 territory: +0.643 EPA and an 85.7% success rate on 14 plays. That is the Ben Johnson menu of play-action and defined reads. The sample is tiny, but it points to how he should be used if he plays: let the scheme create the throw rather than ask him to create it.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle-of-field accuracy
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards produced +0.584 EPA with a 4.8 CPOE, and the middle of the field was his best direction. Those are on-time throws between the linebackers, a veteran's strength. It's 11 attempts, so it's a hint more than a fact.

concerns.title: Collapses when he must create
concerns.body: When the script turned at Green Bay, everything got worse at once: a longer time to throw, more pressure, and a 31.6% bad-throw rate. Trailing by nine or more, he is at -0.463 EPA per play. This isn't new. His non-2017 career is mostly below-average EPA, and it's who he is at this stage.

concerns.title: No vertical threat left
concerns.body: He completed 1 of 4 deep attempts for -0.754 EPA per play, and his tracking CPOE sits at -3.27. Defenses can squat on the short game, which already runs at -0.082 EPA. That limits the ceiling of any offense he runs.

concerns.title: Ball-security slips under duress
concerns.body: Charting gives him two turnover-worthy fumbles, plus an interception, in just 57 dropbacks. His dropbacks overall added up to -3.8 EPA once sacks and scrambles are counted. His bad-throw rate ranks 37th of 45.

trend.note: Two appearances, two opposite outcomes: +6.4 EPA in a controlled Week 3 win over a weak defense, then -5.3 EPA in a Week 5 blowout loss in relief. He hasn't thrown a pass since Williams reclaimed the job in Week 6.

nextGame.headline: Soft Lions pass defense, but QB3 likely won't take a snap
nextGame.body:
On paper, Detroit is a dream for a quarterback. It ranks 26th in pass-defense EPA and 30th in fantasy points allowed to the position, and it leans offenses toward the pass, ranking 2nd in pass funnel. It has also been torched by tight ends: TE1s score 5.7 PPR over their average against it. A 55.5 total indoors points to a shootout. The catch is that Keenum is QB3, listed Out on the site, with Williams entrenched as the starter. He only matters here if two quarterbacks ahead of him go down on a four-day turnaround.

If he were forced in, the details lean his way. Lions safety Chuck Clark (91% of snaps) missed Monday's walkthrough, which would weaken the middle of the field where Keenum does his best work. The counterweight is Detroit's pressure: a 4th-ranked sack rate and 5th-ranked hit rate, with right tackle depth in question as Theo Benedet (75% of snaps) sits questionable. That pressure is exactly what unravelled him at Green Bay.

keyMatchups.title: Middle-field throws vs. thin secondary
keyMatchups.body: Detroit allows a 27th-ranked +0.154 EPA on short passes and is giving up big games to tight ends. That plays straight into Keenum's preferred throws over the middle to Colston Loveland and the slot. Clark's hamstring would only widen the window.

keyMatchups.title: Lions pass rush vs. Benedet's status
keyMatchups.body: Detroit's 8.3% sack rate ranks 4th. Keenum's clean pocket in Week 3 was the foundation of that good game. If Benedet is out and Keenum is ever on the field, quick-game volume becomes mandatory.

nextGame.watch: Whether Keenum is even active on Thanksgiving; any change in his status signals trouble with Williams or the QB2.

restOfSeason.body:
As QB3, the base case is that Keenum throws few or no meaningful passes the rest of the way. The per-game ranges below reflect that, with near-zero volume most weeks. If injuries ever push him into a start, expect the Week 3 template rather than the Week 5 one when Chicago is competitive. That means 25-35 short, on-time throws, a low sack rate, middling yardage, and production propped up by Ben Johnson's under-center play-action. Something like 170-230 yards would be a fair start-week range.

What won't hold is the touchdown efficiency and the +0.19 EPA start. That came against a now-25th-ranked defense with a lead. His sack avoidance and low interception rate are durable career traits. His lack of a deep ball and his fragility when trailing are too.

confidence.note: 53 attempts across one start and a relief outing; he is buried at QB3.
